Breast cancer is a complex disease which is found as the second cause of cancerassociated death among women. Accumulating of evidence indicated that various
factors (i.e., gentical and envirmental factors) could be associated with initiation and
progression of breast cancer. Diagnosis of breast cancer patients in early stages is one
of important aspects of breast cancer treatment. Among of various diagnosis platforms,
imaging techniques are main diagnosis approaches which could provide valuable data
on patients with breast cancer. It has been showed that various imaging techniques
such as mammography, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), positron-emission
tomography (PET), Computed tomography (CT), and single-photon emission computed
tomography (SPECT) could be used for diagnosis and monitoring patients with breast
cancer in various stages. Beside, imaging techniques, utilization of biochemical
biomarkers such as proteins, DNAs, mRNAs, and microRNAs could be employed as new
diagnosis and therapeutic tools for patients with breast cancer. Here, we summarized
various imaging techniques and biochemical biomarkers could be utilized as diagnosis
of patients with breast cancer. Moreover, we highlighted microRNAs and exosomes as
new diagnosis and therapeutic biomarkers for monitoring patients with breast cancer.
KEYWORDS
biomarker, Breast cancer, diagnosis, imaging technique, therapy
1 | INTRODUCTION
Breast cancer is found as one of major health public problems among
various women which a variety of factors such as genetical and
envirmental factors could affect on initiation and progression of it
(Singletary, 2003). Early detection and monitoring of patients in
response to various types of therapies are important aspects of breast
cancer therapy (Barber, Jack, & Dixon, 2004). The utilization of imaging
techniques is one of main approaches for detection and assessment
response to therapy in patients with breast cancer (Khalkhali, Mena,
& Diggles, 1994). Multiple lines of evidence indicated that various
imaging techniques such as mammography, MRI, PET, CT, and SPECT
could be employed as effective tools for assessment patients with
various cancer such as breast cancer, giloma, oral cancer, and

et al., 2017; Khanmohammadi, Mir, Baniebrahimi, & Mirzaei, 2017;

new biomarkers in patients with breast cancer patients has provided
an interesting landscape (Duffy et al., 2017). It has been showed that
a variety of biochemistry biomarkers (i.e., measurement of enzymes,
hormones, and expression profiles of mRNAs, microRNAs). Recently,
MicroRNAs (miRNAs) and exosomes have been emerged as new
diagnostic and therapeutic biomarkers for breast cancer patients
(Santos, Ribeiro, Sarian, Ortega, & Derchain, 2016). These molecules
play critical roles in breast cancer pathogenesis via targeting a variety
of cellular and molecular pathways involved in breast cancer
pathogenesis (Kurozumi et al., 2017). It has been showed that
alteration of miRNAs expression (up/down regulation) could be
affected on initiation and progression of various cancers such as
breast cancer (Gholamin et al., 2017; Kurozumi et al., 2017; Mirzaei,
Fathullahzadeh, et al., 2017; Moridikia, Mirzaei, Sahebkar, & Salimian,
2017). Here, we summarized various imaging techniques are used
for detection and monitoring patients with breast cancer. Moreover,
we highlighted utilization of various biomarkers such as measurement
of enzymes, miRNAs, and exosomes as diagnostic and therapeutic
biomarkers for patients with breast cancer.
2 | IMAGING TECHNIQUES AND BREAST
CANCER
Breast cancer is one of important malignancies worldwide which has
accounted as the most cancer among women. Early detection and
monitoring of patients are found as main aspects of breast cancer
therapy (Weigel & Dowsett, 2010). Breast cancer could be diagnosed
by monitoring of patients with imaging techniques or symptoms such
as pain or a palpable mass. It has been showed; the monitoring healthy
subjects could contribute to detection of small tumors which could
lead to progression of breast cancer (Weigel & Dowsett, 2010). Among
of various techniques, imaging techniques have been emerged as
powerful tools for detection and monitoring response to therapy in
patients with breast cancer (Table 1) (Alcantara, Leal, GarciaBocanegra, & Garcia-Martin, 2014). Mammography is known as gold
standard techniques for detection of breast cancer patients which
are associated with various benefits such as high sensitivity and
specificity, inexpensive, and well tolerated (Wellings, Vassiliades, &
Abdalla, 2016). It has been showed that using of mammography
could reduce 19% breast cancer mortality. Besides, various benefits
of mammography, there are some limitations which are associated
with using this technique such as pain and anxiety, false alarms, and
radiation risks (Wellings et al., 2016). Hence, it seems that utilization
of new techniques with better properties are needed.
Ultrasounds is other major imaging techniques which are known as
other most common method for diagnosis and monitoring response to
therapy in breast cancer (Ozmen et al., 2015). Besides, mammography,
using of ultrasound is required for the management and diagnosis of
breast pathology (Ozmen et al., 2015). The utilization of ultrasound are
associated with various advantages (e.g., it does not use ionizing
radiation, and high sensitivity), which have provided it as powerful
diagnosis tools for detection of breast tumors in young women and
pregnant and breastfeeding women (Alcantara et al., 2014). Ultrasound techniques such including Ultrasound contrast and Elastography are also applied for breast intervention, and for the placement
of harpoons (Alcantara et al., 2014).
In a study, Jia et al. (2014) assessed breast tumor angiogenesis
by three-dimensional contrast enhanced ultrasound (3D-CEUS) and
dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI)
score systems as diagnosis platforms in 35 benign and 148 malignant
breast tumors. They results indicated that 3D-CEUS score system
could be used as an effective diagnosis plathform for evaluation of
tumor angiogenesis in patients with breast cancer. Their results
showed that this score system shows a well association with various
tumor perfusion and vascular characteristics such as microvessel
density (MVD), vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), and matrix
metalloproteinases (MMP-2, MMP-9) expression (Jia et al., 2014).
MRI is found as other important diagnostic tools for breast cancer.
This technique could be used for various aspects of breast cancer
treatment including monitoring of response to therapy, monitoring
high risk patients, assessment of breast cancer metastasis, and study of
tumor recurrence (Mann, Kuhl, Kinkel, & Boetes, 2008). The provided
data by MRI, could suggested various actions (e.g., breast discharge,
staging of breast cancer, evaluation of microcalcifications, premalignant lesions, and residual tumor in operated patients) to clinicians
(Sardanelli et al., 2010). These properties led to introduced MRI as a
suitable diagnosis technique for patients with breast cancer (Mann
et al., 2008; Sardanelli et al., 2010).
The mentioned techniques including mammography, ultrasounds,
and MRI could be employed as effective tools for detection and
monitoring patients with breast cancer (Alcantara et al., 2014). On the
other hands, these techniques are associated with various limitations
such as lacks of sensibility. Hence, radiologist has efforted to introduce
new techniques which could overcome to the current limitations
(Alcantara et al., 2014). It has been showed that utilization of external
substances called contrast agents which are able to improve the
sensibility of images in the region of interest, could be effective
platforms for diagnosis and monitoring patients in early stages of
various cancers such as breast cancer (Alcantara et al., 2014). The using
of contrast agents could enhance the quality and the follow-up of
molecular processes at the cellular and molecular levels of the region
under assessment. The gadolinium- and iodine-based structures are
known as common contrast agents which could be used for MRI and
mammography (X-ray), respectively (Alcantara et al., 2014).
PET and SPECT are other imaging techniques which could be used
for diagnosis breast cancer patients. PET technique uses radioactive
isotopes which emit positrons (e.g., 18F, 15O, 13N, and 11C) whereas

SPECT technique uses isotopes which emit gamma photons, including
99mTc, 123I, or 125I (Benard & Turcotte, 2005).
In a study, Uematsu et al. (2005) assessed the efficacy of PET and
SPECT imaging techniques in 15 patients with bone metastases of
breast cancer. They results indicated that the sensitivity for diagnosing
bone metastases was 85% for SPECT and 17% for PET, specificity of
SPECT and PET were 99% and 100%, and accuracy were 96% and
85%, respectively. They revealed that SPECT was classified the bone
metastases as 92% of metastases as osteoblastic and 35% of
metastases as osteolytic, whereas PET was classified 6% of metastases
as osteoblastic and 90% of metastases as osteolytic. These findings
suggested that SPECT and PET could be used for diagnosis breast
cancer patients with bone metastasis (Uematsu et al., 2005).
Multiple lines of evidence indicated that imaging techniques could
provide effective information on breast tumor morphology and
functional and metabolic processes within the tumor at various levels
(Alcantara et al., 2014). It has been showed that the sensitivity of
the various imaging techniques is varied depending on the type of
biomarkers applied in signaling the vital processes. These studies
suggested that imaging techniques could be employed for diagnosis
and monitoring response to therapy in patients with breast cancer
(Alcantara et al., 2014).
3 | BIOCHEMICAL MARKERS AND BREAST
CANCER
The utilization of various imaging techniques is associated with several
limitations such as expensive, lack of sensitivity, specificity (Alcantara
et al., 2014). Hence, it seems that introducing new biomarkers which
could overcome to the related limitations of imaging techniques are
required. The employing of various biomarkers is known as one of
important aspects of diagnosis and monitoring patients with breast
cancer (Duffy et al., 2017). The suitable biomarkers could contribute to
better understanding of cellular and molecular pathways involved in
breast cancer pathogenesis (Duffy et al., 2017). These findings could
help to designing effective therapeutic approach and monitoring
response to treatment in patients with breast cancer. Several studies
indicated that a variety of biochemical biomarkers including proteins
(i.e., Her2, ER, and Ki67), mRNAs (i.e., ER α,E Rβ, and ERR γ), enzymes
(i.e., CEA and TSGF), and microRNAs (i.e., miR-21, miR-10b, miR-155,
and miR-145) could be used as diagnostic biomarkers for detection
and monitoring breast cancer patients (Duffy et al., 2017; Kurozumi
et al., 2017) (Table 2).
The human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) is one
of important proteins involved in breast cancer pathogenesis (Iqbal,
2014). HER2 is found as a member of the epidermal growth factor
receptor family which has tyrosine kinase activity (Schrohl, Pedersen,
Jensen, Nielsen, & Brunner, 2011). This receptor could be involved in
the regulation of cell growth, survival, and differentiation via targeting
multiple signal transduction pathways. It has been showed that
dimerization of the receptor could lead to auto-phosphorylation of
tyrosine residues within the cytoplasmic domain of the receptors
(Iqbal, 2014). These events could initiate various cellular and molecular
signaling pathways which could contribute to cell proliferation and
tumorigenesis (Weigel & Dowsett, 2010). The up regulation and
amplification HER2 have been observed in 15 -30% cases of breast
cancers and 10 -30% cases of gastric/gastroesophageal cancers

In a study, Soliman and Yussif (2016a) assessed the utilization of
Ki-67 as prognostic and diagnostic biomarkers for monitoring 107
patients with breast cancer. They also investigated the estrogen
receptor, progesterone receptor, and HER2 in patients with breast
cancer. Their results indicated that 44, 23, 15, and 25 subjects were
classified as luminal A, luminal B, HER2 subtype, and triple-negative
(TN), respectively. They showed that in No luminal A patients levels
of Ki-67 were higher than 15%, and their recurrence was 20%. In
luminal B group, Ki-67 levels were higher than 15% and recurrence
was 39% in 69% of patients. In HER2 subtype, in 34% of cases, Ki-67
levels were higher than 15% and recurrence was 40%. Finally, in
triple-negative subjects, in 60% of cases, Ki-67 levels were higher
than 15%, and recurrence was observed in 32% of patients. These
findings suggested that levels of Ki-67 could be applied as predictive
biomarkers for monitoring patients with breast cancer (Soliman &
Yussif, 2016a).
Besides HER2, estrogen receptor (ER), and progesterone
receptor (PR) could be used for classification of breast tumor
subtyping (Dai, Xiang, Li, & Bai, 2016). The steroid hormone,
estradiol, have critical roles in the initiation and progression of breast
cancer. It has been showed that various breast cancers could start
out as estrogen dependent and express the ER (Dai et al., 2016).
Among of various subtypes of ER, ER α is known as main ER subtypes
in the mammary epithelium which has important tasks in mammary
gland biology and in progression of breast cancer (Li et al., 2010). The
following binding of estrogen to ER α, the ligand-activated ER α could
be translocated to the nucleus and bind to the responsive element
in the promoter. These actions via promoting gene transcription
could be associated with stating of a variety of cellular and molecular
pathways involved in the progression of breast cancer (McDonnell
& Norris, 2002). Multiple lines of evidence indicated that estrogen
and ER could contribute to metastasis of breast cancer. Estrogen
signaling could affect on epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT)
and ER α signaling has interaction with various EMT regulators such
as Snail and Slug (Saha Roy & Vadlamudi, 2012). ER α c o u l db i n dt o
the promoter of metastasis tumor antigen (MTA) 3 which could
inhibit Snail. Snail is known as a gene which could affect on EMT
transition (Fujita et al., 2003). ER α are able to regulation of Slug
transcription via making of a co-repressor complex including HDAC1
(histone deacetylase 1) and N-CoR (nuclear receptor co-repressor)
(Ye et al., 2008). ER β,s i m i l a rt oE Rα could be involved in estrogen
signaling. Evolving evidence indicated that up regulation of ER β
could decrease cell proliferation and it could be had anti-proliferative
(tumor suppressor) functions (Speirs et al., 2004; Strom et al., 2004).
Down regulation of ER β was observed in metastatic breast cancer,
and up regulation of ER β expression could be related with less
metastatic condition and proliferating tumors (Jarvinen, PeltoHuikko, Holli, & Isola, 2000; Skliris et al., 2003). These findings

be employed as effective predictive biomarkers for detection and
monitoring patients with breast cancer. Table 2 listed various
predictive biomarkers for detection and monitoring patients with
breast cancer.
4 | MIcroRNAs AND EXOSOMES AS
DIAGNOSTIC BIOMARKERS FOR BREAST
CANCER
MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are known as small non-coding RNAs that
involved in the regulation of the various target genes at the posttranscriptional phase (Fathullahzadeh, Mirzaei, Honardoost, Sahebkar,
& Salehi, 2016; Golabchi et al., 2017; Masoudi, Mehrabian, & Mirzaei,
2017; Mirzaei, Masoudifar, et al., 2017; Simonian, Mosallayi, & Mirzaei,
2017). These molecules act as epigenetic regulators and play critical
roles in various biological processes such as development, angiogenesis, growth and differentiation (Hashemi Goradel et al., 2017;
Mashreghi et al., 2017; Mirzaei et al., 2016; Rabieian et al., 2017;
Rashidi, Malekzadeh, Goodarzi, Masoudifar, & Mirzaei, 2017). It has
been showed that deregulation of miRNAs are related with initiation
and progression of various diseases such as cancer, cardiovascular,
stroke, and diabetes (Hoseini et al., 2017; Mirzaei, 2017; Mirzaei,
Ferns, Avan, & Mobarhan, 2017; Mirzaei, Momeni, et al., 2017;
Mohammadi, Goodarzi, Jaafari, Mirzaei, & Mirzaei, 2016). Evolving
evidence indicated that miRNAs via targeting a variety of cellular and
molecular pathways could be involved in breast cancer pathogenesis
(Kurozumi et al., 2017). Recent reports showed that expression profiles
of miRNAs could be associated with tumor aggressiveness, response to
treatment and patient outcome in breast cancer (Zhang et al., 2017).
One of important aspects of breast cancer is the identification of
intrinsic subtype of the primary tumor. It has been showed that for
each intrinsic subtype of breast tumors must be used specific
treatment regimen. Several reports revealed that each intrinsic
subtypes of breast cancer have different miRNA expression profiles
(Kurozumi et al., 2017) (Table 2). Hence, it seems that the assessment
of expression profiles of miRNAs could be used as effective candidates
for diagnosis and monitoring patients with breast cancer.
In a study, Park et al., investigated a panel of circulating miRNAs
as diagnostic biomarkers for monitoring 11 patients with ER positive
breast cancer (ER+/HER2−) using microarray and qRT-PCR (Park et al.,
2014). Moreover, they assessed the relationship between the
expression levels of circulating miRNAs and clinical outcomes of
ER positive metastatic breast cancer. Their results indicated that
expression levels of various miRNAs including miR-1280, miR-1260,
and miR-720 were up-regulated in blood samples of cancer patients.
Moreover, they showed that Among 37 metastatic breast cancer
patients, miR-1280 (known as a circulating tRNA-derived miRNA)
levels significantly were down regulated after treatment in patients
who received systemic therapy. These results proposed that expression profiles of various miRNAs could be used as diagnostic biomarkers
for patients with breast cancer (Park et al., 2014). It has been showed
that a variety of miRNAs including Let-7, miR-34c, miR-200c, miR-183,
miR-16, and miR-203 could be involved in various stages of breast
cancer such as breast tumor-initiating cells via affecting on several

In a study, Shimono et al. (2009) assessed the expression levels

These findings that deregulation of these miRNAs involved in

and metastasis. It has been showed that this cluster via affecting on

anticipate in metastasis of breast cancer cells (Ahmad et al., 2011;

In a study, Zhang et al. (2017) assessed the expression profiles
of various miRNAs in metastatic breast cancer. Their results showed
that the plasma levels of miR-200c and miR-141 were up regulated in
Foxp3 heterozygous Scurfy mutant. They confirmed that expression
of miR-200c and miR-141 could be modulated by a FOXP3-KAT2B
axis in breast cancer cells, and plasma levels of miR-200c and miR-141
could be used as diagnostic biomarkers for detection patients with
early stage of breast cancer metastasis (Zhang et al., 2017).
Besides miR-200 family, deregulation of other miRNAs such as
miR-34c, miR-106b-25 cluster, miR-30a, and miR-30c via targeting
various cellular and molecular involved in EMT (e.g., TWF1, VIM) could
contribute to metastasis in breast cancer cells (Bockhorn et al., 2013;
Cheng et al., 2012; Smith et al., 2012; Yu et al., 2012).
These studies confirmed that deregulation of various miRNAs play
key roles in initiation and progression of breast cancer. Hence, it seems
that utilization of these miRNAs could be introduced as suitable
diagnostic and therapeutic biomarkers for patients with breast cancer.
Exosomes are other candidates which could be employed as
diagnostic and therapeutic biomarkers for detection and monitoring of
patients with breast cancer (Jia et al., 2017). Exosomes are known as
biological nano-vehicles which could transfer a variety of cellular and
molecular signals to recipient cells (Banikazemi et al., 2017; Saeedi
Borujeni et al., 2017). These signals have major roles in various
physiological events (Mirzaei, Sahebkar, Jaafari, Goodarzi, & Mirzaei,
2017; Moradian Tehrani et al., 2017). Exosomes transfer their signals
via targeting their cargos (i.e., proteins, mRNAs, and miRNAs) to
recipient cells (Mirzaei, Sahebkar, et al., 2017; Saadatpour, Fadaee,
et al., 2016). Multiple lines of evidence revealed that exosomes
and their cargos could be involved in pathogenesis of various cancers
such as breast cancer (Jia et al., 2017). Hence, it seems that exosomes
and their cargos could be used as diagnostic and therapeutic
biomarkers in breast cancer.
Among of various cargos which could be carried by exosomes,
miRNAs have been emerged as major cargos with big roles in patients
with breast cancer (Sempere, Keto, & Fabbri, 2017). It has been
showed that exosomal miRNAs have critical function in various
diseases such as breast cancer (Sempere et al., 2017).
In a study, Hannafon et al. (2016) assessed the plasma levels of
various exosomal miRNAs in patients with breast cancer. Their results
showed that exosomes released from breast cancer cells are enriched
with various miRNAs including miR-21 and miR-1246. The evaluation
of plasma levels of these exosomal miRNAs showed that these
molecules were up regulated in plasma of patients with breast cancer.
These findings suggested that exosomal miRNAs could be used as
diagnostic candidates for detection and monitoring patients with
breast cancer (Hannafon et al., 2016).
In other study, Singh, Pochampally, Watabe, Lu, and Mo (2014)
indicated that exosomal miR-10b could induce metastasis in breast
cancer cells. Their results revealed that exosomal miRNAs could be
carried among different cell lines by direct uptake. They showed that
exosomal miR-10b was up regulated in MDA-MB-231 cells (as
metastatic breast cancer) than non-metastatic breast cancer cells or
normal breast cells. Moreover, they indicated that nSMase2 or
ceramide could induce the secretion of exosomal miR-10b whereas
ceramide inhibitor could inhibit this action. miR-10b are able to inhibit
the expression of its target genes (e.g., HOXD10 and KLF4) which play
key roles in breast cancer metastasis. These results proposed that
exosomal miRNAs relaeased from metastatic breast cancer cells could
have critical roles in progression of metastasis in breast cancer cells.
Hence, exosomal miRNAs could be introduced as new diagnosis and
therapeutic options for patients with breast cancer (Singh et al., 2014).
Developmental Endothelial Locus-1 (Del-1) is one of important
proteins involved in cancer (Beckham et al., 2014). This proteins is
known as an extracellular matrix protein which has three N-terminal
epidermal growth factor-like domains and factor V C domains, C1, and
C2 (Schurpf et al., 2012). It has been showed that this protein could
express by endothelial cells during embryonic vascular development and
induces the adhesion of endothelial cells via its interaction with other
proteins such as integrin receptors (Hidai et al., 1998; Schurpf et al.,
2012). Several studies indicated that Del-1 could be expressed in various
cancers such as breast cancer (Aoka et al., 2002; Sun et al., 2010). These
results proposed that Del-1 could be used as cancer-specific biomarker
for various human cancers such as breast cancer. Recently, in a study,
Chae et al. (2015) assessed the expression levels of exosomal Del-1 in 10
patients with early stages of breast cancer (stages I and II). Their results
revealed that the levels of exosomal Del-1 was significantly up regulated
in patients with breast cancer at all stages than other groups. These
findings suggested that exosomal Del-1 could be utilized as new
diagnostic biomarker for patients with breast cancer (Chae et al., 2015).

5 | CONCLUSION
Breast cancer is one of important cancers among women which is
known as the second most common cancer worldwide. Diagnosis
of breast cancer is main aspects of breast cancer therapy. Multiple
lines of evidence indicated that a variety of approaches and
biomarkers have potential to are used as diagnostic approaches
for detection and monitoring patie nts with breast cancer. Imaging
techniques including mammography, MRI, SPECT, PET, and CT
and development of them could be employed for diagnosis and
monitoring breast cancer patien ts. Despite, more development of
imaging techniques, utilization of them are associated with various
limitations such as expensive and sensitivity. Hence, it seems that
identification new tools for diagnosis of breast cancer patients are
required. It has been showed that utilization of new biomarkers
such as evaluation of expression le vels of various proteins (i.e., ER,
Ki67, PR, and HER2) and vario us molecules (miRNAs and
exosomes) have opened new opportunity for diagnosis and
monitoring patients with breast cancer.
